To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human striatum has a complex and diverse population of NMDA receptors with different subunit compositions and that this diversity may contribute to the selective vulnerability of striatal neurons to ischemic and excitotoxic insults.

(1) All human striatal neurons express NR1 mRNA; (2) GAD67‐, SOM‐, and SP‐positive neurons express NR2A mRNA; (3) ChAT‐ and SP‐ positive neurons express NR2B mRNA; (4) SOM‐ and ChATA‐ positive neurons express moderate NR2D mRNA, whereas GAD67‐ positive neurons express low and ENK ‐positive neurons express no NR2D mRNA.
all neurons of the human striatal complex have NMDA receptor, but different populations express different combinations of subunits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of the brain.
the molecular biology of the NMDA receptor, a glutamate‐gated ion channel that is involved in synaptic transmission and plasticity, and is implicated in a number of neurologic disorders.
the development of new methods for the detection and quantification of NMDA receptors and the study of their expression in the human striatal neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human striatum is a heterogeneous structure with respect to its neuronal populations and that the expression of NR1 and NMDA receptor NR2 subunits is not uniform.
all human striatonigral and striatopallidal neurons express NMDA receptors composed of NR1 and at least one NR2 subunit.

the NMDAR is an important component of the excitatory synapse and its function is regulated by the expression of the NR2 subunit isoforms, which may have a role in the regulation of the excitability and synaptic plasticity of the striatal neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NMDA receptor in the striatum is a complex structure, and that the subunit expression pattern is different in different neuronal populations, and also that the subunit composition of NMDA receptors in human striatum is similar to that in the rat striatum.
the striatum is a highly complex region with respect to the expression of NMDAR subunit mRNas.
all neurons of the human striatal complex have NMDA‐type glutamate receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NMDA receptors of striatal interneuronal populations are different from each other as well as from the NMDA receptor expressed by striatonigral projection neurons.
all neurons in the striatum express the same NMDA receptor, but the composition is different between interneurons and medium spiny neurons.
the striatal neurons are not all the same, and the differences in their NMDA receptors may contribute to the differences in the way they function.
